question_types_in_exam.summary: UP Board Class 12 History mein 6 types: MCQ (1 mark), VSA (2 marks, 30 words), SA (5 marks, 80 words), LA (10 marks with OR, 200-250 words), Historical Dates (1 mark each, 10 dates), Map (2 marks each, 5 items).

types.mostly_from: Sare 10 attempt karo — no negative marking. 4 sub-types: direct choice, match the following, assertion-reason, statement-based. Elimination method use karo jab confused ho.

chapters.name: Bricks, Beads and Bones — The Harappan Civilisation (Eenten, Mankein tatha Asthiyaan)
topics: Harappan civilisation — origins, extent, chronology (2600-1900 BCE)
First city — story of Harappa's discovery (1921, Dayaram Sahni; Mohenjodaro 1922, R.D. Banerjee)
Urban centres — Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Chanhudaro, Lothal, Kalibangan, Dholavira, Rakhigarhi
Town planning — Citadel + Lower Town, grid pattern, drainage system (sabse advanced), Great Bath at Mohenjodaro, granary
Subsistence — agriculture, animal husbandry, fishing, trade
Crafts — bead-making (Chanhudaro), seal-making, pottery, metallurgy (bronze)
Script (undeciphered), weights, seals
Social differences — burials, luxuries
Contact with other civilisations — Mesopotamia (Meluha)
Decline theories — climate change, Aryan invasion (rejected), river shifts, deforestation
Archaeology — Cunningham (first DG ASI), John Marshall, R.E.M. Wheeler
Kalibangan — evidence of ploughed field, fire altars
Dholavira — Gujarat, water reservoirs, first-discovered signboard

chapters.name: Kings, Farmers and Towns — Early States and Economies (Raja, Kisan aur Nagar)
topics: Political and economic history from 600 BCE to 600 CE
Mahajanapadas — 16 in 6th century BCE (Magadha emerged dominant)
Mauryan Empire (321-185 BCE) — Chandragupta Maurya, Bindusara, Ashoka (268-232 BCE)
Ashoka's inscriptions — Dhamma, major rock edicts, pillar edicts, Brahmi and Kharoshti scripts
James Prinsep — first deciphered Brahmi and Kharoshti (1838)
Gupta period (320-550 CE) — Chandragupta I (320 CE founded), Samudragupta (Harishena's Prayaga Prashasti), Chandragupta II
Harishena — court poet of Samudragupta, composed Prayaga Prashasti
Land grants — copper plate inscriptions (Tamra-patra)
Agrarian society — taxes, crops, trade
Coinage — punch-marked coins, gupta gold coins (dinars)
Urban centres — Pataliputra, Ujjain, Mathura
Sources — inscriptions, coins, Arthashastra, Indica (Megasthenes), Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta), Mrichhakatikam (Shudrak)

chapters.name: Kinship, Caste and Class — Early Societies (Bandhutva, Jaati tatha Varg)
topics: Mahabharata as a source — critical edition by V.S. Sukthankar (1919-66, 47 years)
Ved Vyasa — composer of Mahabharata
Kinship — patriliny vs matriliny, gotra rules, marriage (8 forms)
Caste (varna-jati) — 4 varnas (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra), creation myth from Purusha sukta
Beyond 4 varnas — untouchables, forest dwellers, hunters
Women — Gandhari, Draupadi, Kunti — agency and restrictions
Dynasties — Kuru, Panchala, Pandavas
Manusmriti as dharma-shastra source
Sanskrit vs Prakrit in Mahabharata

chapters.name: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings — Cultural Developments (Vichark, Vishwas aur Imaratein)
topics: Sacrificial religion — Vedic religion (Rig Veda, yajnas)
6th century BCE — upheaval; rise of heterodox sects
Buddhism — Gautam Buddha (born 563 BCE Lumbini, enlightenment Bodh Gaya, first sermon Sarnath, mahaparinirvana Kushinagar)
4 Noble Truths, 8-fold path, Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma), Sangha
Jainism — Mahavira (24th Tirthankara), 5 Mahavratas (Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha)
Vaishnavism and Shaivism (brief)
Sanchi Stupa — discovered 1818, built by Ashoka, toran gateways, sculpture depicting Buddha symbolically (footprints, wheel, empty throne, Bodhi tree) — no anthropomorphic form initially
Amaravati Stupa (destroyed), Bharhut Stupa
Stupa architecture — anda (dome), harmika, yashti, chhatra
Bhaja caves, Karle caves — rock-cut architecture
Shah Jehan's Begum Shahjehan Begum of Bhopal helped preserve Sanchi

chapters.name: Through the Eyes of Travellers — Perceptions of Society (Yatriyon ke Nazariye)
topics: Al-Biruni (11th cent, Uzbek, came with Mahmud of Ghazni 1017) — wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' in Arabic; translated Sanskrit works into Arabic
Ibn Battuta (14th cent, Moroccan, came to India 1333 during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign) — 'Rihla' in Arabic; described cities, Indian postal system, coconut/paan/slaves

Francois Bernier (17th cent, French physician, came 1656-68 in Aurangzeb's reign) — 'Travels in the Mughal Empire' in French; critical of Mughal state, compared India with Europe, concept of Oriental Despotism
Abdur Razzaq — visited Vijayanagara (not in main travellers list but context)
Other travellers — Marco Polo, Domingo Paes

chapters.name: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions — Changes in Religious Beliefs (Bhakti, Sufi Paramparayein)
topics: Bhakti movement — devotion to personal god, rejection of caste/ritual
Alwars (Vaishnava — Vishnu worshippers, Tamil Nadu, 6-9th cent) — 12 saints including Andal (female), Nammalvar
Nayanars (Shaiva — Shiva worshippers, Tamil Nadu) — 63 saints
Saguna Bhakti (with form) — Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas), Surdas (Krishna), Meerabai (Krishna)
Nirguna Bhakti (formless) — Kabir, Guru Nanak
Sikhism — Guru Nanak (founder), Guru Govind Singh founded Khalsa Panth (1699)
Sufism — Islamic mysticism; Silsilas (Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri, Naqshbandi)
Chishti order — Shaikh Moinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi)
Sufi concepts — tariqa (path), sama (devotional music), khanqahs
Sufi and Bhakti similarities — love, devotion, challenge to orthodoxy

chapters.name: An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara — Hampi (Ek Samrajya ki Rajdhani — Vijayanagara)
topics: Vijayanagara empire (1336-1565) — founded by Harihara and Bukka on banks of Tungabhadra
Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva (Krishnadeva Raya 1509-29 greatest), Aravidu dynasties
Battle of Talikota (1565) — decline
Capital Hampi — UNESCO World Heritage
Discovery — Colonel Colin Mackenzie (1800)
Architecture — Virupaksha temple, Vithala temple (musical pillars), Lotus Mahal, Elephant stables, Ramachandra temple (royal temple)
Water works — Hiriya canal, Kamalapuram tank, step-wells, Tungabhadra river use
Administrative system — nayaka system, amara-nayakas (military chiefs)
Trade — long distance with Portuguese at Goa (1510 onwards)
Sources — Domingo Paes, Fernao Nuniz, Abdur Razzaq accounts

chapters.name: Peasants, Zamindars and the State — Agrarian Society and the Mughal Empire (Kisan, Zamindar aur Rajya)
topics: Ain-i-Akbari — composed by Abul Fazl (1590s), part of Akbarnama; detailed account of administration
Abul Fazl — court historian of Akbar; Akbarnama in 3 volumes (Ain is 3rd volume)
Agrarian society 16-17th centuries — jins-i-kamil (cash crops), peasants (raiyat, khud-kasht, pahi-kasht)
Land revenue — Todar Mal's settlement (Zabti system)
Mansabdari system — Zat (personal rank) + Sawar (cavalry rank), pay in jagir form
Zamindars — intermediaries, collected revenue
Women in agrarian society
Forests and tribes — jangli territory
Trade — hundis, sarrafs (bankers), Indian Ocean trade
Taj Mahal — built by Shah Jahan (1631-53) for Mumtaz Mahal in Agra

chapters.name: Colonialism and the Countryside — Exploring Official Archives (Upniveshvad aur Dehat)
topics: Late 18th century — EIC rise, Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Buxar (1764)
Revenue systems — Permanent Settlement (Bengal, 1793, Lord Cornwallis) — zamindars became landlords
Sunset Law — if zamindar didn't pay revenue by sunset of specified date, estate auctioned
Ryotwari system (Madras, Bombay) — Thomas Munro; direct settlement with ryot
Mahalwari system (NW Provinces, Punjab) — R.M. Bird, Holt Mackenzie
Subsidiary Alliance — Lord Wellesley (1798)
Doctrine of Lapse — Lord Dalhousie
Santhal rebellion (1855-56) — Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, Bhairav; led to creation of Damin-i-Koh
Indigo rebellion — Bengal 1859-60, ryots vs British planters
Deccan riots — 1875, peasants vs moneylenders
Francis Buchanan — surveyor, reports on Indian countryside
Deccan Riots Report (1878), Fifth Report (1813)

chapters.name: Rebels and the Raj — The Revolt of 1857 and its Representations (Vidrohi aur Raj)
topics: 1857 Revolt (Sepoy Mutiny / First War of Independence) — 10 May 1857 began in Meerut
Causes — economic (revenue exploitation), political (Doctrine of Lapse), religious (cartridge issue — cow/pig fat), social
Major leaders and centres:
Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar (symbolic)
Kanpur — Nana Sahib, Tantya Tope
Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal, Birjis Qadr
Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai
Bihar — Kunwar Singh
Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
Focus on Lucknow in NCERT
Visual representations — British paintings (e.g., 'Relief of Lucknow'), Indian nationalist reinterpretation
Suppression — British brutality, siege of Delhi, Lucknow
Consequences — EIC abolished (1858), direct Crown rule, Proclamation of Queen Victoria
V.D. Savarkar's book 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' (1909) — called it first war of independence

chapters.name: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement — Civil Disobedience and Beyond
topics: Gandhi's return from South Africa (1915)
Early satyagrahas: Champaran (1917, indigo), Kheda (1918, revenue), Ahmedabad mill strike (1918)
Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar)
Khilafat-Non-Cooperation movement (1920-22) — leaders: Ali brothers (Shaukat + Mohammad); withdrawn after Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922)
Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34) — Dandi March (12 Mar-6 Apr 1930, Salt Satyagraha)
Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931)
Second Round Table Conference (1931, London)
Quit India Movement (Aug 1942) — 'Do or Die'; Bharat Chhodo
Subhash Chandra Bose — INA, addressed Gandhi as 'Father of the Nation' first (1944 radio)
Newspapers as historical sources — The Hindu, Amrita Bazar Patrika, Young India, Harijan
1931 as focal year in NCERT

chapters.name: Framing the Constitution — The Beginning of a New Era (Samvidhan ka Nirmaan)
topics: Constituent Assembly formed — first sitting 9 Dec 1946; Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (provisional chairman), then Dr. Rajendra Prasad (permanent)
Objective Resolution — moved by Jawaharlal Nehru (13 Dec 1946), adopted 22 Jan 1947
Drafting Committee — chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Aug 1947)
Constitution adopted — 26 Nov 1949, came into force 26 Jan 1950
Major committees — Union Powers (Nehru), Provincial (Patel), Drafting (Ambedkar), Fundamental Rights
Women members — 15 including Sarojini Naidu, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, Sucheta Kripalani, Hansa Mehta, Durgabai Deshmukh, Begum Aizaz Rasul, Dakshayani Velayudhan (1st Dalit woman)
Key debates — national language (Hindi vs Hindustani vs English), federalism, minority rights, adult franchise
Preamble — 'soul of the Constitution' (K.M. Munshi's phrase); sometimes Fundamental Rights also called soul
Features — sovereignty, democracy, secularism, fundamental rights, DPSP, parliamentary system, federal with unitary bias, independent judiciary

Sources — Domingo Paes, Fernao Nuniz, Abdur Razzaq accounts
chapters.frequently_asked: Vijayanagara capital VSA (2026 — Hampi). Vijayanagara establishment VSA (2024 — Harihara-Bukka 1336). Vijayanagara water needs SA (2024, 2025). Vijayanagara admin + water LA (2026). 1336 AD common date. 1510 AD Portuguese Goa common date.

chapters.name: Peasants, Zamindars and the State — Agrarian Society and the Mughal Empire (Kisan, Zamindar aur Rajya)
chapters.book: Themes in Indian History — Part II
important_topics: Ain-i-Akbari — composed by Abul Fazl (1590s), part of Akbarnama; detailed account of administration
Abul Fazl — court historian of Akbar; Akbarnama in 3 volumes (Ain is 3rd volume)
Agrarian society 16-17th centuries — jins-i-kamil (cash crops), peasants (raiyat, khud-kasht, pahi-kasht)
Land revenue — Todar Mal's settlement (Zabti system)
Mansabdari system — Zat (personal rank) + Sawar (cavalry rank), pay in jagir form
Zamindars — intermediaries, collected revenue
Women in agrarian society
Forests and tribes — jangli territory
Trade — hundis, sarrafs (bankers), Indian Ocean trade
Taj Mahal — built by Shah Jahan (1631-53) for Mumtaz Mahal in Agra
chapters.frequently_asked: Ain-i-Akbari author MCQ (2024 — Abul Fazl). Mansabdari system SA (2026). Taj Mahal location MAP (2025 — Agra). 1605 AD (Akbar's death/Jahangir) common date.

chapters.name: Colonialism and the Countryside — Exploring Official Archives (Upniveshvad aur Dehat)
chapters.book: Themes in Indian History — Part III
important_topics: Late 18th century — EIC rise, Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Buxar (1764)
Revenue systems — Permanent Settlement (Bengal, 1793, Lord Cornwallis) — zamindars became landlords
Sunset Law — if zamindar didn't pay revenue by sunset of specified date, estate auctioned
Ryotwari system (Madras, Bombay) — Thomas Munro; direct settlement with ryot
Mahalwari system (NW Provinces, Punjab) — R.M. Bird, Holt Mackenzie
Subsidiary Alliance — Lord Wellesley (1798)
Doctrine of Lapse — Lord Dalhousie
Santhal rebellion (1855-56) — Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, Bhairav; led to creation of Damin-i-Koh
Indigo rebellion — Bengal 1859-60, ryots vs British planters
Deccan riots — 1875, peasants vs moneylenders
Francis Buchanan — surveyor, reports on Indian countryside
Deccan Riots Report (1878), Fifth Report (1813)
chapters.frequently_asked: Subsidiary Alliance MCQ (2024 — Wellesley). Permanent Settlement year MCQ (2024, 2025 — 1793). Santhal leaders MCQ (2025 — Sidhu-Kanhu). Francis Buchanan VSA (2024). Sunset Law SA (2025). Buchanan's survey value SA (2025). Santhal rebellion LA (2025). 1793 AD, 1855, 1875 common dates.

chapters.name: Rebels and the Raj — The Revolt of 1857 and its Representations (Vidrohi aur Raj)
chapters.book: Themes in Indian History — Part III
important_topics: 1857 Revolt (Sepoy Mutiny / First War of Independence) — 10 May 1857 began in Meerut
Causes — economic (revenue exploitation), political (Doctrine of Lapse), religious (cartridge issue — cow/pig fat), social
Major leaders and centres:
Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar (symbolic)
Kanpur — Nana Sahib, Tantya Tope
Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal, Birjis Qadr
Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai
Bihar — Kunwar Singh
Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
Focus on Lucknow in NCERT
Visual representations — British paintings (e.g., 'Relief of Lucknow'), Indian nationalist reinterpretation
Suppression — British brutality, siege of Delhi, Lucknow
Consequences — EIC abolished (1858), direct Crown rule, Proclamation of Queen Victoria
V.D. Savarkar's book 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' (1909) — called it first war of independence
chapters.frequently_asked: Jhansi leader 1857 MCQ (2026 — Rani Lakshmibai). Kanpur challenger 1857 VSA (2025 — Nana Sahib). Savarkar's book MCQ (2025). Begum Hazrat Mahal location MAP (2026 — Lucknow). 10 May 1857 common date.

chapters.name: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement — Civil Disobedience and Beyond
chapters.book: Themes in Indian History — Part III
important_topics: Gandhi's return from South Africa (1915)
Early satyagrahas: Champaran (1917, indigo), Kheda (1918, revenue), Ahmedabad mill strike (1918)
Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar)
Khilafat-Non-Cooperation movement (1920-22) — leaders: Ali brothers (Shaukat + Mohammad); withdrawn after Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922)
Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34) — Dandi March (12 Mar-6 Apr 1930, Salt Satyagraha)
Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931)
Second Round Table Conference (1931, London)
Quit India Movement (Aug 1942) — 'Do or Die'; Bharat Chhodo
Subhash Chandra Bose — INA, addressed Gandhi as 'Father of the Nation' first (1944 radio)
Newspapers as historical sources — The Hindu, Amrita Bazar Patrika, Young India, Harijan
1931 as focal year in NCERT
chapters.frequently_asked: Gandhi movements MCQ (2026 — all). Quit India start MCQ (2025 — Aug 1942). Non-cooperation withdrawal MCQ (2025 — Chauri Chaura). Father of Nation first used MCQ (2025 — Subhash Bose). Khilafat leaders VSA (2026 — Ali brothers). Dandi March SA (2026). Gandhi-Irwin Pact SA (2024). Gandhi's contribution LA (2026). Rise of Indian nationalism LA (2024). Quit India essay LA (2024). Champaran MAP (2026 — 1st satyagraha). Dandi MAP (2024 — salt law). Jallianwala Bagh MAP (2024). Chauri Chaura MAP (2025). Lahore 1929 MAP. 1919, 1942 common dates.

chapters.name: Framing the Constitution — The Beginning of a New Era (Samvidhan ka Nirmaan)
chapters.book: Themes in Indian History — Part III
important_topics: Constituent Assembly formed — first sitting 9 Dec 1946; Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (provisional chairman), then Dr. Rajendra Prasad (permanent)
Objective Resolution — moved by Jawaharlal Nehru (13 Dec 1946), adopted 22 Jan 1947
Drafting Committee — chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Aug 1947)
Constitution adopted — 26 Nov 1949, came into force 26 Jan 1950
Major committees — Union Powers (Nehru), Provincial (Patel), Drafting (Ambedkar), Fundamental Rights
Women members — 15 including Sarojini Naidu, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur, Sucheta Kripalani, Hansa Mehta, Durgabai Deshmukh, Begum Aizaz Rasul, Dakshayani Velayudhan (1st Dalit woman)
Key debates — national language (Hindi vs Hindustani vs English), federalism, minority rights, adult franchise
Preamble — 'soul of the Constitution' (K.M. Munshi's phrase); sometimes Fundamental Rights also called soul
Features — sovereignty, democracy, secularism, fundamental rights, DPSP, parliamentary system, federal with unitary bias, independent judiciary
chapters.frequently_asked: Objective Resolution MCQ (2026 — Nehru). Soul of Constitution MCQ (2024 — Preamble OR Fundamental Rights — depends on interpretation). Constituent Assembly objectives SA (2024). Adult franchise democracy SA (2025). National language characteristics SA (2026). Constitution basic features LA (2025, 2026). 16 Aug 1946 (Cabinet Mission plan) common date.

exam_day_rules.extra_time_note: 15 minute reading time (paper padhne ke liye) — likhna allowed nahi is time mein.

answer_sheet_rules: sequence_note: Sequence follow karna zaroori nahi — Section E (dates+map) pehle bhi attempt kar sakte ho (easy 20 marks).
mcq_attempt_all: Sare 10 MCQ attempt karo — no negative.
dates_sirf_1_line: Q25 mein date diya gaya hai — sirf 1-2 line mein event likho. Paragraph likhne ki zaroorat nahi.
map_item_split: Har map item = 1 (location/dot) + 1 (name) = 2 marks. Dono sahi honey chahiye full marks ke liye.

pen_rules.note: allowed_colors: ['Blue', 'Black'] pencil_use: Map ke liye pencil se symbol banao, naam pen se likho. Diagrams (Stupa structure, Harappan town layout) bhi pencil se better. map_attachment: Supplied outline map ko question paper se fadke, usmein 5 places ko dot (●) + naam se identify karke, answer book ke saath MAZBOOTI se attach karna COMPULSORY.

exam_writing_rules.diagram_rules: illustrate_with_sketch: Instructions mein NAHI likha hota (Geography se alag) par Harappan town planning, Stupa, Vijayanagara water system jaise topics mein sketch banao — extra marks milte hain. headings_subheadings: LA (200-250 words) mein 4-5 sub-headings use karo — 'Kaaran', 'Prakriti', 'Mahatva' etc. word_limits: 30 / 80 / 200-250 — respect karo. Zyada likhne se time waste. partial_marking: True partial_marking_note: SA/LA mein jitne points sahi honge, un sab ke marks milenge. Ek galat point se baaki cut nahi hote. hindi_english_mix: Naam/technical terms English mein (Permanent Settlement, Mansabdari, Drainage system) + explanation Hindi mein chalega.
